subject: Go-to-close signal runway and test anchors
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@healthprime.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + success signals for evaluation (first pass)

Laura — great to meet last week. Per our call I pulled together an initial mutual action plan focused on the evaluation phase and the concrete acceptance tests that will drive a go/no-go decision. Attached is HP_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) and a short PDF with proposed acceptance test cases. High level ask: please review the success signals below and confirm which items HealthPrime needs to own vs. Redwood owns.

Key success criteria (proposed):
- Functional: 90%+ intent classification concordance on the sample QA dataset (50k rows) and >85% precision on the top-10 clinical entity extractions.
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 300ms for 512-token requests under trial traffic profile.
- Reliability: >=99.5% availability during business hours (US Eastern) for the pilot window.
- Safety / accuracy: false-positive rate for high-risk labels flagged and reviewed within 24 hours in pilot logs.

Exit gates (what constitutes a pass to move from evaluation -> onramp):
1) Evidence pack delivered: final smoke test artifact, concordance report, latency histogram, and sampling of 200 flagged examples with root-cause notes.
2) Security checklist: signed SSO integration test, SOC2 evidence stub uploaded to the shared Drive.
3) Ops readiness: runbook for incident triage and an agreed fallback model variant for QoS fallback.

Acceptance tests (examples in attached):
- End-to-end smoke (ingest -> inference -> postprocess) with seeded edge cases (pass if no regression >5% vs. baseline).
- Load step test to reach expected concurrency for your throughput profile; 95p latency must remain under target.
- Randomized sample of 1,000 results assessed by clinical SME for concordance.

Proposed timeline (tight):
- May 14: HP confirms owners and supplies anonymized sample dataset
- May 19: Redwood delivers iteration 1 of acceptance-test results and evidence pack
- May 25: Joint review; if pass, schedule Dedicated capacity onboarding window

Next steps: can you confirm by Friday which of the success criteria need adjustment for HealthPrime compliance? If you prefer, we can convert the spreadsheet to a live mutual action plan in HubSpot (I included the deal link).

Thanks — Sean

Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: HP_MAP_v1.xlsx, type: spreadsheet)
(attachment: acceptance_test_cases.pdf, type: pdf)

From: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@healthprime.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + success signals for evaluation (first pass)

Sean — thanks for the clear draft. Quick notes from my side after an initial pass with the product and security teams: we agree with the general structure and the three exit gates, but need two adjustments: (1) tighten the safety review cadence — we require flagged high-risk labels to be triaged within 12 hours during the pilot, and (2) add a data retention and deletion verification step under the security checklist (we can provide the policy doc).

Also: the clinical SME review will be run by our internal QA team; can you confirm whether Redwood will supply the audit sampling tooling (we prefer reproducible sampling seeds) or we should run sampling and share results?

We will aim to provide the anonymized sample dataset by May 15 but need assurance the dataset will only be used for evaluation and deleted after completion per our policy.

Laura Gomez
Head of Product Operations — HealthPrime
(HealthPrime contact: procurement@healthprime.com)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Laura's notes. Two immediate asks for alignment before I reply:
1) Marissa — can the QA team enable a reproducible sampling tool and produce the sampling seed + script we'll include in the evidence pack? Estimated effort?
2) Ben — procurement/security asked for a data deletion verification step. Can we add a short, automated proof-of-delete routine (log + hash) to the test checklist and a KMS audit snippet in the Drive? Also note HealthPrime wants a 12-hour triage SLA for high-risk flags during pilot (we proposed 24).

I propose we accept the 12-hour triage for pilot but document an escalation ladder (1h paging window) in case severity escalates. If there are operational concerns, flag them now.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@healthprime.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Finalized MAP items + evidence pack contents and acceptance-test owners (action required)

Laura — thanks for the quick review last week. Based on your feedback we updated the MAP and acceptance tests; attachments in the Drive folder now include the sampling script, proof-of-delete checklist, and the revised acceptance_test_cases.pdf. Summary of the agreed changes below (finalized unless you object within 48 hours):

Agreed updates
- Safety triage SLA: pilot = 12 hours for high-risk labels; post-pilot SLA to be negotiated during contract (default 24h).
- Proof-of-delete: Redwood will run a proof-of-delete routine against the evaluation dataset within 48 hours of completion and provide logs + hash; HealthPrime will supply the deletion confirmation receipt for its local copy.
- Sampling: Redwood will supply the reproducible sampling script (seeded) and include the seed in the evidence pack. QA review will be run by HealthPrime.
- Acceptance thresholds (final): intent concordance >= 90% on sample dataset; extraction precision >= 85%; 95p latency <= 300ms under the specified load profile. If any single critical metric misses by >7% vs. threshold we will treat as a fail and trigger root-cause and remediation.

Deliverables and owners (short):
- HealthPrime: provide anonymized sample data (due May 15) and run SME review of the sampled results.
- Redwood: run acceptance tests, provide evidence pack (due May 19), execute proof-of-delete, and provide runbook + fallback variant.

Next steps (action items):
- Laura: confirm you will upload the sample dataset to the Drive folder by EOD May 15 and confirm deletion policy document.
- Marissa: attach sampling script to Drive, add readme with seed and instructions.
- Ben: prepare the KMS audit snippet and add proof-of-delete automation to the checklist.

If we get the items by the dates above, we remain on track for the May 25 joint review and a potential close window in early June. If any timeline slips, we will rebaseline the MAP in HubSpot and update the deal milestone.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachments uploaded to Drive: HP_MAP_v1.xlsx, acceptance_test_cases.pdf, sampling_script.py)
